title: Onboardable Network Proofflow & Fast Retention — PRD Sketch
content:
Summary:
This is a working PRD sketch for an "onboardable" proofflow and compact evidence retention mode targeted at customer-managed networking (private deployments). The goal: provide a minimal, queryable audit package that enables fast approval gating, maintains regulatory-proof retention for required windows, and supports a low-latency UX for operator workflows (canary changes, emergency rollbacks).

Context & why now:
- Customers running Redwood Private frequently request faster handoff/approval cycles for VPC changes or edge connector updates. Current approval and evidence collection is bulky and slows onboarding and incident triage.
- Compliance teams want tamper-evident artifacts but not a multi-gig forensic archive per small change.
- Product objective: reduce approval-to-accept time by ~50% for routine network/operator changes while preserving provable auditability for 1+ years (configurable).

Key user personas:
- Customer network operator: needs a simple, fast approval UI and compact evidence to show to internal auditors.
- Redwood operator: validates inbound customer attestation and can escalate to security when anomalies occur.
- Compliance reviewer: requires immutable evidence with chain-of-custody metadata, queryable without heavy tooling.

Goals (measurable):
- Median approval cycle time for standard VPC change: from 12h to <=6h (within 3 months of launch).
- Evidence payload size per change: target <= 200KB (typical) using compact serialization and sample hashing.
- Support configurable retention stencils: quick-retain (30d), standard (1y), extended (7y).
- Provide SDK/API so customers can programmatically attach attestations and retrieve evidence.

Non-goals:
- Do not replace full forensic export for major incidents — we will keep a heavier archive path for those cases.
- Not addressing tenant-level cryptographic key management beyond integration points (KMS/HSM).

Proposed design overview:
1) Evidence Capsule: a compact JSON-LD style bundle that includes minimal fields required for audit: change-delta, requester identity (OID/email), operator assertion (free text), timestamps (request/approve/commit), references to network config artifacts (hashes), optional sample telemetry snapshot (up to N KB), and a signature blob (Redwood-signed + optional customer signature).
2) Approval Gate Modes: fast-path (operator-only approval), policy-path (policy checks + customer ok), manual-path (customer-signed). Each gate exposes an API to attach pre-check evidence and to return structured accept/reject reasons for UI display.
3) Retention Engine: tiered retention with TTL and cold-storage policy. Small capsules are kept in fast index for the chosen policy window; at threshold we materialize a compressed forensic record (on-request) but not retained by default.
4) UX: inline approval flow in Console and API: preview change -> auto-lint checks -> evidence capsule preview -> one-click approve (or request more info). Support canary toggles and auto-fallbacks.

Evidence capsule (example fields — serialized as compact JSON text):
- capsule_id: uuid
- change_summary: text diff (minimized)
- requester: email/identity-id
- operator_note: free text
- pre_checks: [list of check ids + pass/fail] (compressed)
- artifact_refs: [hash1, hash2] (store manifest pointing to full blobs in customer or Redwood archive)
- telemetry_digest: base64(SHA256 snapshot) (optional small sample: up to 16KB)
- approvals: [ {actor, role, time, signature_reference} ]
- redwood_signature: reference to signed manifest (kms-key-id)
- retention_tier: quick|standard|extended

API & integration notes:
- POST /v1/private/evidence-capsules -> returns capsule_id and preview (for console).
- GET /v1/private/evidence-capsules/:id -> returns capsule metadata and pointers to full artifacts (if allowed).
- PATCH /v1/private/evidence-capsules/:id/approve -> attach signature or approve token.
- Webhooks: on-approve/on-reject/on-expire to customer endpoint (configurable).
- SDK: small client helpers (python/ts) to assemble minimized diffs and compute telemetry_digest locally before upload.

Approval flow (fast-path example):
1) Operator creates change bundle in Console.
2) System runs auto-checks (connectivity smoke, ACL lint, required tags).
3) A capsule is produced (<=200KB).
4) Operator approves via Console (or API) -> capsule marked approved and redwood_signature attached.
5) Change applied; post-commit snapshot generated and linked.

Audit log shape & query patterns:
- Index keys: capsule_id, requester_id, approver_id, affected_tenant_id, change_time, retention_tier, tags.
- Queries expected: "list approvals for tenant X in window Y", "fetch capsule for change Z", "verify signature chain for capsule Z".
- Provide CLI helper to produce a human-readable audit brief for compliance meetings.

Retention & compliance considerations:
- Retention tiers configurable per-customer and per-operator profile.
- Default regulatory minimal retention: 1 year (standard).
- For exports/subpoena, support on-demand expansion: reconstruct full forensic archive from stored artifact_refs + customer-side artifacts if available.
- Tamper-evidence: Redwood signs capsule manifest using a per-tenant signing key (backed by KMS). Provide proof-of-signature verification endpoint.

Observability & KPIs:
- Approval latency distribution (fast-path vs manual).
- Evidence size distribution and % under target.
- Number of on-demand forensic exports.
- Rate of auto-failures from pre_checks.

Operational concerns & cost tradeoffs:
- Storage cost for quick-indexed capsules (SSD tier) vs cold storage (object+glacier).
- Need retention enumeration UI to let customers tune tiers.
- Backfill migration: customers with current bulky logs need an importer that can derive compact capsules from existing forensic archives.

Security & privacy:
- Sensitive fields redacted by default in UI (full artifacts only available via properly-scoped API tokens).
- Tenant encryption-at-rest; Redwood signature keys in KMS with strict access controls.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (internal + 2 beta customers): implement capsule format, console preview, simple fast-path approvals. (6 weeks)
- Beta (10 customers): add retention tiers, signatures, SDK helpers, webhooks. (8–10 weeks)
- GA: full approval gate types, exporter, forensics-on-demand, SSO/KMS integrations. (4–6 months)

Open questions / trade-offs (TODO):
- Must the capsule store a compressed patch (delta) or a normalized canonical snapshot? pros/cons of both.
- How to handle cross-tenant approvals and multi-operator sign-off? quorum?
- Exact TTL defaults for regulated sectors (finance/healthcare) — coordinate with compliance team.
- Backward compatibility: how to map existing audit log schemas to capsule format automatically?

Immediate next steps & owners:
- Product: finalize capsule schema v0 (owner: Laura Chen) — due 2024-11-05.
- Eng infra: prototype storage index and sign/verify pipeline (owner: Miguel Torres) — spike 3 weeks.
- Applied ML / Optimize: define sampling heuristics for telemetry_digest (owner: Anya Patel) — 2 weeks.
- SRE/Security: KMS key policy draft and signature rotation SOP (owner: Samir Gupta) — 3 weeks.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight; aim is to make approvals practical for day-to-day network ops. Expect multiple iterations particularly around schema and retention economics.
- Feedback ask: prioritize the UX for console approval vs API-first customer integration? Any hard regulatory retention requirements we should bake into default tiers?

Appendix: example capsule (compact representation as text):
{"capsule_id":"c5b8ef76-9a1d-4a3f-8d2f-0bd9e3f7a9b2","requester":"alice@acme.com","change_summary":"add route 10.0.0.0/16 -> peering-123","pre_checks":"[connectivity:pass,acl:pass,tag:warn]","telemetry_digest":"sha256:ab12...","approvals":["operator:alice@acme.com:2024-10-21T17:12:03Z:signature-ref:sgn-88"],"redwood_signature":"kms:arn:...","retention_tier":"standard"}
